transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Redwood CSM), Nina Kapoor (Emerald Head of ML), Tom O'Leary (Product Lead), Jasmine Park (Security), Ravi Menon (Data Eng)

Summary:
- Weekly POC sync focused on quality evaluation and identified regressions on a small prompt set.
- Walkthrough of recent eval scores, discussion of guardrails and scoring thresholds, plan to run Dedicated latency/cost bench, and schedule security deep-dive.
- Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics covered:
- Prompt-set variations and metrics (precision/recall, hallucination rate, guardrail triggers)
- Scoring rubric and regression detection thresholds
- Tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated for throughput/cost, VPC/KMS for security
- Action items and timeline for pilot expansion

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this to 45 mins. quick roll call?
[00:07] Nina (Emerald): nina here, tom here, jasmine and ravi also on.
[00:12] Samira: great. diego do you want to kick off with the quality numbers?
[00:16] Diego (Redwood SE): yeah, sure. so we ran the latest prompt set (v3) against the 2k eval set last night. overall precision held at about 88%, but we saw a regression in the summarization prompts — rouge-L dropped ~6 points vs last week, and hallucination rate went up on clinical-cases.
[00:35] Tom (Emerald): hmm ok, can you remind us which model variant that was? hosted or the quantized dedicated candidate?
[00:40] Diego: that was the hosted baseline (redwood-curie-ish, internal alias rwd-curie-v2). the dedicated q4_0 quant candidate actually did a little better on hallucination but had slightly higher latency on long contexts. i think some of the kernel-path differences cause the behavior — kv cache and attention splits got slightly different peformance.
[01:02] Nina: interesting — do you think it's a prompt drift issue or model degradation from the new tokenizer/quant changes?
[01:08] Diego: early signal points to prompt sensitivity — a few prompts that used conditional phrasing are now being classified as 'instruction' vs 'context' by the model, which changes completions. also quantization can amplify small tokenization shifts.
[01:22] Ravi (Emerald): we did push a small dataset rebalancing last week, could that interact? we did increase the weight of outpatient notes in the eval sample.
[01:29] Diego: yeah that could surface different failure modes. worth re-running with the previous sample distribution to isolate.
[01:34] Samira: let's note that as an experiment. diego, add to your bench runs.
[01:38] Lena (Redwood CSM): quick question on thresholds — what threshold do you want us to alert on for regression detection? current alert is set to 5% absolute drop but if rougel drops 6 that's a noisy signal maybe.
[01:52] Nina: we care about user-facing hallucination first — so set a guardrail on hallucination rate, say >3% absolute increase triggers a review. for rouge-l maybe make it windowed, like sustained 4-pt drop over two runs.
[02:06] Samira: makes sense. we'll update the eval runner to emit both immediate alerts for hallucination spikes and rolling-window alerts for score drift.
[02:15] Tom: can we also include a human-sample review for any flagged prompts? we need triage flow.
[02:20] Samira: yes, diego will export a triage queue with examples, and we can annotate via the shared spreadsheet.
[02:27] Diego: on the guardrails side, we added an output filter that blocks responses containing certain PI I terms and medical advice phrases — it's catching about 70% of the easy cases but misses some entailed hallucinations. we should tune the classifier threshold and maybe add a reranker step.
[02:46] Jasmine (Security): on that note, we need to ensure logs and PII redaction meet our internal policy. can you confirm what is stored in the debug logs on Redwood hosted?
[02:55] Samira: by default hosted debug logs redact PII and we have redact rules, but for the pilot we're using verbose logging for analysis with redaction enabled; we can also turn on KMS-wrapped log storage on Dedicated/Private.
[03:08] Jasmine: ok please send the compliance packet — SSO/SAML config, SOC 2 scope, KMS options, and data retention policies.
[03:15] Samira: will do. lena i'll attach the packet from our security team.
[03:18] Lena: yep i'll share.
[03:20] Ravi: about Dedicated — you mentioned latency increased for longer contexts. how big is the delta? our production SLO is 300ms p50 for interactive use.
[03:28] Diego: on the Dedicated q4_0 path we saw p50 ~380ms for 1k-context runs vs hosted p50 ~340ms, but cost per token dropped ~22%. with batching and KV caching tuning we can get p50 down by ~30-40ms.
[03:44] Tom: cost savings sound good but latency matters for our UX. is there a way to have mixed routing? keep critical endpoints hosted and bulk inference on Dedicated?
[03:52] Samira: yes that's exactly the smart routing option — route by policy (latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive) with automatic fallback. we can prototype split routing for your endpoints.
[04:03] Diego: also consider model variants — a slightly smaller model for interactive paths gives you better latency with acceptable quality. we can run A/B on a small percent.
[04:12] Nina: ok let's plan an A/B with 10% of traffic to the smaller variant for two weeks and monitor percents.
[04:17] Samira: noted. diego will set up the eval hooks.
[04:20] Diego: one more thing — we found a reproducible failure mode on the 'med-summarize' prompt where the model hallucinates non-existent medication names. i've added five failing examples to the spreadsheet.
[04:31] Ravi: saw those — i'll pull the raw logs and send them to you; may be tokenizer edge-case.
[04:35] Samira: good. for fix path we have three options: prompt rewrite (fast), reranker/guardrail (medium), or model/quant changes (slower). prioritize prompt and reranker and we'll run the model change in parallel if needed.
[04:49] Tom: timeline?
[04:50] Samira: we aim to ship prompt updates and reranker tuning by end of next week, bench Dedicated runs by end of week after, and security packet by early next week.
[04:59] Lena: i'll update the pilot timeline doc after this call.
[05:03] Nina: sounds good — can you also include the acceptance criteria for expansion? we need a clear gate.
[05:09] Samira: yes proposed acceptance criteria: hallucination rate <2%, no regression >4 pts on rouge-l across the primary test set, latency p50 <350ms for interactive routes, and security checklist complete. we can iterate.
[05:25] Jasmine: one last ask — do you support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/private?
[05:30] Samira: yes, we support customer KMS/HSM for Private and can integrate with cloud KMS for Dedicated; i'll include config notes in the packet.
[05:39] Tom: ok let's recap next steps.
[05:41] Samira: recap: Samira send eval spreadsheet and patch prompt set; Diego run Dedicated 1k latency/cost bench + re-run with previous sample distribution; Diego export triage queue for flagged prompts; Jasmine provide compliance artifact list; Ravi share logs and 5 failing cases; Lena update timeline and attach security packet.
[05:58] Nina: thanks everyone.
[06:00] Samira: thanks all — meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps small, some product names slightly mis-transcribed (rwd-curie-v2), KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cash. Links shared during call: eval spreadsheet (internal link), security packet (to be attached).
